statement: An optimal Kantorovich dual pair can be represented by a Y-convex potential phi and its X-transform. Where complementary equality is differentiable, grad(phi)=grad_x(Phi); if y->grad_x(Phi) is a diffeomorphism, inversion uniquely yields the Monge map.
assumptions: An optimal finite-valued Kantorovich dual pair exists and both expectations are defined.
Complementary-support equality is differentiable in x at the point being evaluated.
For map recovery, y->grad_x(Phi)(x,y) is a diffeomorphism onto a set containing grad(phi)(x).
pass_criteria: Every paper-specific order implication in the universal normalization certificate is discharged.
An independent exact-rational finite-domain checker validates feasibility, objective monotonicity, and the triple-transform identity.
Exact optimal multidimensional nonquadratic examples in dimensions 2, 4, and 8 recover their maps through the stated inverse.
A non-twist negative control fails uniqueness for the intended reason.
The cumulative verifier exits nonzero if any criterion fails.
